title: POC decision log — latency/cost profiles and prompt sweeps
content:
Context:
This doc captures the decision log and experimental notes for a time-boxed POC with Customer X (enterprise commerce). Goal: pick a deployable model/config that meets 99th-percentile latency <= 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), 95% of quality baseline (their BART-based internal baseline on NPS answers), and reduces per-request GPU token cost by >= 40% vs their current hosted baseline.

Summary of objective and constraints:
- Primary metrics: p99 latency, throughput (qps), model memory footprint, and answer-quality (weighted F1 + human pass rate).
- Target hardware for Dedicated: single A10G (16GB) for staging; target private on customer infra: V100-16GB.
- Allowed model formats: FP16, INT8 (static), and dynamic per-layer 8-bit. No custom kernel development for the POC timeline.
- Prompt pipeline must support optional retrieval + instructions, so KV cache reuse for multi-turn is important.

Model candidates evaluated:
- open-7b-instruct (baseline candidate) — comparable to Llama2-7b in capability but faster in our infra.
- mosaic-ml-mpt-7b-instruct — lighter attention, slightly lower quality on long-context Q/A.
- flan-t5-xl (converted to causal variant) — strong structured output, higher latency per-token on decode-heavy tasks.
- smaller tuned 4.2b BLOOM variant (customer-tuned checkpoint) — highest compression potential but risk of hallucination.

Quantization strategies tested (short-hand names used in results):
- fp16: native half precision (baseline for accuracy).
- int8-dynamic: dynamic quantization applied to matmuls at runtime (lower quality risk in some layers).
- int8-static-perlayer: calibration-based static quant with per-layer scale/zero adjustments (longer prep, better stability).
- q4_kv-cache: 4-bit key/value cache packing while keeping activations fp16 to preserve generation quality in multi-turn.
- prune-attention-heads: drop top-k low-salience heads per-layer (experiment only).

Prompt/pipeline tuning experiments:
- Minimal instruction vs expanded instruction templates (short vs verbose).
- Two-stage pipeline: retrieve top-3 docs -> extractive chunking -> generation with source attribution.
- Caching strategy: warm KV cache for multi-turn sessions, cold start penalty measured separately.
- Temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) and top-p (0.9) kept constant for comparison.

Experiment matrix (subset):
- Model x Quantization x PromptTemplate x Hardware. Each cell run across 3 seeds and 5 sample workloads: shortFAQ (avg 24 tokens), ticket-summary (avg 96 tokens), product-explain (avg 140 tokens), multi-turn-support (3 turns, 220 tokens cumulative), retrieval-heavy (doc concat 512 tokens).
- Measured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, mean generation token quality (automatic scores), and a small human eval (n=30) for pass/fail on helpfulness.

Key empirical findings (high level):
1) Latency vs quality tradeoffs:
   - fp16 open-7b-instruct: p99 on A10G for shortFAQ = 110ms (meets p99 target), helpfulness pass rate = 86% vs internal baseline 95% (quality gap).
   - int8-static-perlayer open-7b-instruct: p99 reduced to 78ms, mem usage down by ~28%, helpfulness pass rate = 83% (small quality drop but within acceptable delta for routing).
   - q4_kv-cache gave best memory reduction for multi-turn flows (effective working set down by ~42%) while preserving fp16 activations; p99 for multi-turn stable.

2) Model-specific notes:
   - mpt-7b-instruct quantized to int8-dynamic: very fast single-token latency but more frequent truncation/hallucination on long-context due to attention differences; not recommended for retrieval-heavy flows.
   - flan-like model: stronger at structured outputs and low hallucination, but decode latency per-token ~25% higher even after int8-static; likely requires 2x capacity for equivalent throughput.
   - customer-tuned 4.2b: when combined with int8-static-perlayer, cost was lowest (estimated per-request GPU token cost reduction ~55%), but human pass rate varied widely by prompt style (70–88%). Needs more prompt tuning and possibly light fine-tuning on safety prompts.

3) Prompt engineering outcomes:
   - Short, well-scoped instructions substantially improved helpfulness for smaller models (delta +8–12%).
   - For retrieval-heavy prompts, adding a short instruction to cite sources reduced hallucination score by ~14% but increased latency by 20–40ms due to longer context.
   - Two-stage pipelines (extractive then generate) reduced hallucination and improved conciseness at the cost of an additional 30–50ms wall-time; overall end-to-end latency still within target for most flows if quantized.

Operational considerations observed during POC runs:
- Cold-start token penalty: models using int8-static-perlayer had slightly higher cold-start latency (calibration tables loaded), so warmup hooks recommended on Dedicated capacity during rollout.
- Model compatibility: our serving runtime handled q4_kv-cache with minimal changes, but mpt attention kernel regressions required a fallback to fp16 for some sequences. Add to model verification checklist.
- Monitoring: need both token-level cost traces and prompt-set quality monitors. We observed cases where automated scores were stable but human pass rate dropped (edge prompts).

Recommendations for customer-facing POC rollout:
1) Short-term (MVP, 2–4 week):
   - Deploy open-7b-instruct with int8-static-perlayer on Dedicated (A10G). Use q4_kv-cache for multi-turn endpoints.
   - Use lightweight prompt templates (short instructions + retrieval top-3) and measure human pass rate weekly.
   - Instrument warmup hooks and a pre-warm policy for endpoints with low traffic.

2) Medium-term (4–12 week):
   - Run parallel A/B with customer-tuned 4.2b int8-static-perlayer behind a quality gate (only route specific ticket types). If quality tuning succeeds, shift lower-cost flows to 4.2b.
   - Add constrained decoding penalties to reduce over-generation for tuned small models.
   - Expand human eval set to n=100 per week for regression detection.

3) Risk and mitigations:
   - Risk: int8 quantization regressions on corner-case prompts -> mitigation: auto-fallback to fp16 for flagged prompts and continuous calibration jobs.
   - Risk: cold-start spikes on Dedicated -> mitigation: pre-warm scale-to-zero policy with grace periods and keep-alive micro-pings.
   - Risk: hallucination increase on small tuned models -> mitigation: staged rollout and prompt-set specific safety fine-tuning.

Decision log (actions taken):
- 2025-06-02: Chosen candidate for MVP: open-7b-instruct + int8-static-perlayer, q4_kv-cache enabled for session endpoints. Owner: Michael Chen.
- 2025-06-04: Added short instruction templates as default for helpdesk and product-explain flows. Owner: Priya Nair.
- 2025-06-07: Enabled warmup hook and scheduled nightly calibration job for int8 tables. Owner: Jorge Martinez.

Appendix: Selected raw metrics (median of runs, A10G):
- open-7b-instruct fp16 shortFAQ: p50 22ms / p95 65ms / p99 110ms / mem 9.8GB / human-pass 86%
- open-7b-instruct int8-static shortFAQ: p50 14ms / p95 35ms / p99 78ms / mem 7.1GB / human-pass 83%
- 4.2b-tuned int8-static ticket-summary: p99 62ms / mem 5.2GB / human-pass 80%
- mpt-7b int8-dynamic retrieval-heavy: p99 95ms / mem 6.8GB / human-pass 72% (hallucination flags up)

Notes to follow-up in next sync:
- Run a 2-week expanded human eval on customer-critical prompts (n=200).
- Try hybrid quantization: q4_kv-cache + int8 weights + selective fp16 for attention-softmax on problematic layers.
- Workshop with customer on prompt templates and annotated failure cases (schedule week of 2025-06-16).

Quick checklist for Solutions Eng runbook (what to validate before customer demo):
- [ ] Model verification: generation hygiene, repeatable seeds, limited output length.
- [ ] Quantization sanity: quality delta under 5% for protected prompt set.
- [ ] KV cache validation: multi-turn continuity tests across scaled sessions.
- [ ] Warmup: endpoint warmup script added and verified.
- [ ] Monitoring: token-level cost dashboard + weekly human-eval board linked.
End of doc.
